text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Health insurance companies demand fewer beds in clinics
- Bundestag may delay move to Berlin to 2000 if buildings are not ready
- Coal subvention to be cut in 1997
- SPD not fighting any more over property taxes
- Eastern firms expect slight recovery
- Dieter Philipp becomes new craftwork association president
- Economy on weak growth path
- Jose Ignacio Lopez's resignation expected on Friday
HANDELSBLATT
- Bonn and Paris arguing over EMU
- East German firms somewhat more optimistic
- Kinkel to shut three embassies in 1997. Foreign Ministry to close three western European consulates and three embassies in third world because of budget cuts
- Progress in tax negotiations
- North Rhine Westphalia government to decide on ownership structure of Duesseldorf airport this year
- Lufthansa profits fall
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Genetically altered food will be labelled
- PDS not right for coalition with the Greens - Fischer
- Craftworkers' association president Spaeth recommends consensus course to his successor Philipp
- CeBIT will be the biggest trade fair in the world
DIE WELT
- Lopez about to resign from VW
- SPD charges government with cooking the books
- Health insurance plans for extensive cuts
- Teachers in east Germany must wait further for civil servant conditions.
- Businesses in east cautiously optimistic for next year - survey
- Lopez criticised from the start
- German wholesale and export federation warns of implications of flight of capital from Germany
- Health insurance presents strike list
